item.title: Labour's Bev Craig elected mayor of Greater Manchester, replacing Andy Burnham
item.description: Labour's Bev Craig secures nearly double the number of votes won by Reform UK's Sian Astley.

item.title: Budget to be held in October, Healey announces
item.description: The new chancellor pledged to move money and power out of Westminster, and into every postcode around Britain.

item.title: Burnham faces criticism over plans for mayors to get share of income tax
item.description: Tory mayor Lord Houchen wants to offer a rebate, but the prime minister says it should be reinvested in communities.

item.title: Burnham considers reversing plan to scrap some jury trials
item.description: The prime minister says his "instinct" is to reverse plans by the last PM to limit jury trials in England and Wales.

item.title: High Court upholds decision to allow Chinese mega embassy
item.description: The government has given the green light to the site on the old Royal Mint, near the Tower of London.

item.title: Infantino 'wrong man' to lead Fifa says Burnham as criticism grows
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham says Gianni Infantino is "the wrong man" to lead Fifa as criticism grows of the controversial investment plan.

item.title: MP Diane Abbott readmitted into Labour Party after suspension
item.description: The long-serving MP apologises for past comments and says she has been issued with a "formal warning".

item.title: Wheels could come off Stormont without reform, says Sinn Féin
item.description: The Democratic Unionist Party says it is interested in delivering for the people of Northern Ireland.

item.title: BP puts North Sea business up for sale
item.description: The decision follows a review of BP's operations and is set to end 60 years of production in the region by the oil giant.

item.title: Andy Burnham to give regional mayors share of income tax
item.description: The prime minister says the move will give power to "every postcode" but critics say the plans lack detail.

item.title: Unions to boycott Labour women's conference over trans ban
item.description: The BBC understands the ban goes against long-standing policies on trans inclusion in most unions.

item.title: Council cancels climate emergency declaration
item.description: A Reform UK motion argues the council can improve the local environment without the official pledge.

item.title: Burnham says nuclear sub investment will protect UK and boost jobs
item.description: Speaking ahead of a visit to Barrow-in-Furness, the PM seeks to stress the economic benefits of defence spending.

item.title: Councillor sanctioned in row over 'sexualisation'
item.description: The leader of the Reform UK group at Devon County Council says it was important to raise concerns.

item.title: Burnham says he told Trump UK will be pragmatic about North Sea oil
item.description: Andy Burnham says he told the US president he couldn't ignore North Sea resources when people are struggling.

item.title: Concerns raised over council's £900m debt
item.description: Councillor Patrick Lambert fears taxpayers will be left liable for the authority's debts.

item.title: Jenrick urges Burnham to rule out tax rises to fund social care
item.description: The prime minister has not ruled out tax rises to fund a long-awaited shake-up of social care.

item.title: Welsh holiday home tax rules could be eased after backlash
item.description: The Welsh government is to review the impact of a "modest' cut to the 182-day business rate threshold.

item.title: Bank holds interest rates but says it is ready to raise them if Iran war escalates
item.description: The Bank also expects the economy to grow more than previously forecast this year, although uncertainties remain because of the Iran war.

item.title: Virtual interviews don't show bosses your personality, says Burnham
item.description: Interviews online may not allow young people to "shine" and communicate their "passion", the prime minister says.

item.title: Palestine Action ban to be reviewed by Supreme Court
item.description: The UK's highest court gives Palestine Action's co-founder permission to appeal the government's proscription of the group under anti-terrorism legislation.

item.title: Large rise in offenders sent back to prison, figures reveal
item.description: There has been a large rise in the number of offenders being recalled to prisons in England and Wales.

item.title: Inquiry finds MoD Afghan data breach was foreseeable failure
item.description: The Commons' Defence Committee says in a report that the MoD used secrecy as a "shield" against proper expertise.

item.title: Burnham doesn't rule out tax rises to fix social care
item.description: The prime minister holds cross-party talks as he speeds up review of social care in England.

item.title: Fix palliative care before assisted dying debate, says PM
item.description: Andy Burnham's comments suggest he will not personally back a fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales.

item.title: Gangland hitman who threw acid at Scottish Conservative leader is freed
item.description: Russell Findlay has warned that organised crime groups may still have "unfinished business" with him after learning William Burns would be leaving prison.

item.title: Councillor charged over Nigerian population comment
item.description: Glenn Gibbins, from Sunderland, will appear at South Tyneside Magistrates' Court next month.

item.title: Greens review social media operation as Polanski row rumbles on
item.description: The Green Party is grappling with how to manage its social media following a controversial post by its leader.

item.title: Andy Burnham wants to fix social care - what are the options?
item.description: With Andy Burnham saying he wants to bring "substantial change" to social care in England, BBC Verify looks at what could be done.

item.title: 'Every day I'm just winging it': The families hoping for social care reform
item.description: As Andy Burnham outlines his aim to overhaul social care, BBC News speaks to the families caring for loved ones.

item.title: Laura Kuenssberg: Our exclusive behind-the-scenes access at No 10 as Andy Burnham became PM
item.description: Laura Kuenssberg was given unprecedented access to the new prime minister’s first days in power.

item.title: Andy Burnham's first week pledges - how much do they add up to?
item.description: BBC Verify has looked at how much Burnham's new spending commitments cost and how they will be paid for

item.title: Faisal Islam: The UK's Trump trade deal no longer looks world-beating
item.description: While the US tariffs imposed on the UK are effectively unchanged, other countries now have a better deal.

item.title: Andy Burnham's plan to collaborate with social media creators
item.description: The new prime minister plans to work with influencers and social media creators to get his message out.

item.title: Sackings, cabinet surprises and policies: Burnham's first 24 hours as PM
item.description: The new prime minister enters Number 10 in a flurry of activity - but he is still facing calls for a snap election.

item.title: Who's in Andy Burnham's cabinet?
item.description: An in-depth look at which Labour MPs have been appointed to cabinet roles by new Prime Minister Andy Burnham

item.title: Louise Haigh: Labour power broker behind Burnham's rise
item.description: The Sheffield MP's return to the cabinet comes after she emerged as one of the PM's key political allies.

item.title: Angela Rayner: Cabinet comeback for one of Labour's biggest names
item.description: The potential contender to replace Keir Starmer is now back in the cabinet under Andy Burnham.

item.title: Who is new chancellor John Healey? Labour veteran who quit as defence secretary
item.description: The former defence secretary is seen as a safe pair of hands - and is now in charge of the government's finances.

item.title: Five headaches Andy Burnham will have to deal with as PM
item.description: From defence spending to housing - the next UK leader has a series of challenges to deal with.

item.title: Burnham's 'Manchesterism' got him to No 10 - but will it work for the UK?
item.description: Economics editor Faisal Islam examines whether the north-west city can be a template for the entire country.

item.title: Can Andy Burnham solve the housing crisis?
item.description: BBC Verify has looked at the scale of the housing challenge facing Burnham when he becomes PM.

item.title: Burnham set for No 10: BBC correspondents on what Trump, Putin and others will make of him
item.description: In the US, China, Europe, Russia and elsewhere, how is the UK's expected new prime minister regarded?

item.title: How a rise in ADHD benefits claims is adding to welfare spending challenge
item.description: More than 100,000 people with ADHD as their main condition receive Pip, latest figures show, an increase of 40% since Labour came to power.

item.title: How the leasehold revolution could transform neighbourly relations
item.description: The government wants to abolish leasehold, but replacing it could prove far more complicated

item.title: 'Posh George': Who is aristocrat and convicted criminal at heart of Farage controversy?
item.description: The 32-year-old reported crypto entrepreneur, once convicted of fraud in the US, is a long-time Farage ally.

item.title: Burnham's people: MPs and advisers in line for a job if he gains power
item.description: The key figures likely to be influential if Burnham succeeds in gaining the keys to Number 10.

item.title: What we know about Andy Burnham's policies
item.description: The former Greater Manchester has begun outlining the policies he will pursue as prime minister.

item.title: Key takeaways as Andy Burnham becomes PM
item.description: The new Labour leader has formally taken office and set out his priorities for power in No 10.

item.title: Burnham has big ideas - but what will they cost?
item.description: Every tricky decision and trade off is being watched by the country and the markets at the same time

item.title: Can Burnham's casual style survive contact with No 10?
item.description: When Burnham becomes PM, he'll find it harder to wear the wardrobe that's central to his political brand.

item.title: He'll be the first Andy in No 10 - but his rise to power has been decades in the making
item.description: The outgoing Greater Manchester mayor is lining up a third attempt to be Labour leader following his return to Westminster.

item.title: Analysis: Burnham's policy choices reveal what kind of PM he wants to be
item.description: The new prime minister has begun to set out key policies - starting with a vow to end rough sleeping.

item.title: Burnham does not rule out wealth tax
item.description: The expected next PM says he may have to "ask for a little more" in tax and warns of "difficult" choices.

item.title: Row after Tory bid to make Burnham face MPs before autumn fails
item.description: The Tories have accused Labour of "running scared" after ministers denied them a chance to delay Parliament's summer break.

item.title: Cash-strapped Thames Water poses big test for Burnham
item.description: Despite returning to profit after hiking bills 40%, the deeply troubled company is far from out of the woods.

item.title: Chris Mason: What his first week in power tells us about Andy Burnham
item.description: The fledgling Burnham administration has been seeking to find its feet and make a decent first impression at the same time, the BBC's political editor Chris Mason explains.

item.title: Shapps blocked from standing again for the Conservatives
item.description: Kemi Badenoch tells the BBC she leads a "new party full of new people" as ex-MP is rejected as a candidate.

item.title: Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar set to become a minister in Burnham's government
item.description: It would mean Sarwar leaving the Scottish Parliament and his leader role, then taking up a seat in the House of Lords.

item.title: Chris Mason: Sarwar ministerial role sees promotion of another Starmer critic
item.description: Months after calling on Keir Starmer to quit, the Scottish Labour leader is set to become a minister in Burnham's government, the BBC's political editor writes.

item.title: Burnham tells cabinet to tackle living costs at first meeting
item.description: The new prime minister chaired his first cabinet after announcing a cut to VAT on household electricity.

item.description: Laura Kuenssberg was given unprecedented access to the new prime minister’s first days in power.

item.title: Ruthless plotter? Flip-flopper? Dad dancer? Insiders reveal the real Andy Burnham
item.description: Who is the real Andy Burnham? Laura Kuenssberg talks to more than 20 people who know him to work it out

item.title: Burnham's 'Manchesterism' got him to No 10 - but will it work for the UK?
item.description: Economics editor Faisal Islam examines whether the north-west city can be a template for the entire country.

item.title: The Nowak murder has lit a match under British politics. This is how we got here
item.description: The police response to the murder of Henry Nowak has triggered a heated transatlantic debate.

item.title: Is it harder than ever to be prime minister?
item.description: Discontent with the political class is greater than ever - has the UK become ungovernable?

item.title: Should Glasgow have its own mayor?
item.description: The BBC's David Wallace Lockhart asks if Scotland's largest city should have its own elected mayor.

item.description: Zack Polanski reported to police over guillotine post

item.title: My dog Axel 'wouldn't get on' with Larry the cat, says Burnham
item.description: The PM says he doesn't think his poodle-mix would "get along" with Larry the cat, who has lived at No 10 for 15 years.

item.title: Andy Burnham rules out early election in exclusive BBC interview
item.description: The new prime minister told Laura Kuenssberg that people "voted for a manifesto" that he would honour, when pressed on whether there will be an early general election.

item.description: See inside Andy Burnham's first week in charge, with an exclusive behind the scenes look with Laura Kuenssberg.
